items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: Because he was still -- cussing out Melrose --

ctx.x: -- oh, that was gosh, that -- let me see -- that was after -- was that after? That was during the time of the Rhythm Club, I have to pinpoint that year. The Rhythm Club was in its heyday then, they had moved -- moved from -- it was on 32nd Street, 30 something street, and there was a guy named Hall that came from Chicago, to open the Rhythm Club, George Hall, I think that was his name, he was a bass player. Did you ever hear of his name? But, he opened the Rhythm Club here in New York.

That was the time I met Jelly Roll -- in fact, if I can get back to that year, I think that was, -- that was during the time before I went to Europe with Sam Wooding. Something around in that area, in that time. Because he was still -- cussing out Melrose --
